title: and her Children by Rosie Glen-Lambert and Hailey McAfee at Soho Play...
transcript: This play completely ruined my day, yet it impressed me and has my utmost recommendation. Based on a 1939 Brecht play, and her Children is a modern, mostly solo piece in which Anna Fierling tells the story of how the thing she makes a living defending is also what has ruined her life. As a spokesperson for the NRA, she's made countless controversial town hall appearances including the one that this play is framed as. Anna is sharply rendered, delivering her story in a relentlessly focused manner. And as a single act, there's no breath-catching here — you simply have no choice but to lock in. This is the kind of piece that's meant to make you uncomfortable, and it does so in a few ways. It's not just the dark subject matter, it's the fact that it feels eerily realistic and urgent, and the way that it makes you think. There are quite a few ethical questions posed in here, and while it's easy to judge Anna and the way that she thinks about them, she makes a compelling case that you should be able to relate to her cognitive dissonance. As I said, I did not feel great leaving the show, and for that very reason, I think it's a successful piece. and her Children is running at Soho Playhouse through February 13th. With that, another program for my collection.
